headings: The upgrade most small businesses actually need.
When it's worth it, and when it isn't
We'll show you what you actually need
content.text: Microsoft 365Business PremiumStandard +12% · Premium unchanged The upgrade most small businesses actually need. Business Standard is fine for the basics. Business Premium adds the security and device-management features you actually need to be Cyber Essentials-ready and to actually defend against modern threats. We'll tell you honestly whether the upgrade is worth it for your business, and if it's not, we'll say so. Book a licence audit →See the comparison ↓ Business Premium £18.10 per user / month · price unchanged Standard is going up 12%, Premium isn't. The upgrade gap is now just £6.56/user/month instead of £7.80. Best time to upgrade is right now. What you get Six big upgrades over Standard Each one would cost more as a separate add-on. Bundled together they're cheaper and they actually integrate properly. 🛡️ Microsoft Defender for Business Next-gen endpoint protection across PC, Mac and mobile. Real ransomware defence, not just AV. 📱 Microsoft Intune Manage every device from one console. Zero-touch deploy, remote wipe, policy enforcement. 🔐 Azure AD Premium P1 Conditional Access, MFA enforced everywhere, self-service password reset. 📧 Proper anti-phishing layer Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (Plan 1): safe links, safe attachments, real-time scanning of inbound mail. Much better than the Business Standard baseline. 🔒 Information Protection Label sensitive documents, encrypt automatically, prevent forwarding outside your org. 💾 Data Loss Prevention Stop sensitive data leaving by accident. Block uploads of card numbers, NI numbers, client lists. Standard vs Premium The line-by-line comparison Feature Business Standard Business Premium Cost per user / month £11.54 (was £10.30, +12%) £18.10 (unchanged) Office apps + email ✓ ✓ Teams + SharePoint ✓ ✓ Endpoint protection Built-in basic Defender for Business: full EDR Device management None Microsoft Intune included Conditional Access + MFA Limited Azure AD P1: full policy engine Phishing + safe-links Basic Defender for O365 Plan 1 Information protection No Yes (labels + encryption) Data Loss Prevention No Yes Cyber Essentials ready Not without add-ons Yes, out of the box Reality check: With Standard going up 12% and Premium holding firm, the upgrade gap is shrinking to ~£6.56/user/month. And if you're buying Business Standard plus AV plus a separate MDM tool, you're already paying more than Premium would cost, for worse integration. Honest take When it's worth it, and when it isn't Upgrade if You handle sensitive client data (legal, healthcare, finance) You need Cyber Essentials certification Staff use personal devices for work email You'd struggle if a stolen laptop wasn't wiped within the hour You currently pay for a separate AV / MDM / DLP tool Maybe skip if Under 3 staff and all work-issued devices You have no client data and no compliance obligations You already have full-stack security elsewhere Cost is genuinely the blocker: Standard + good practice is OK Need a licence audit? We'll show you what you actually need 20 minutes. We'll review your current setup, tell you whether Premium is worth the upgrade, and how to roll it out cleanly.
